data.title: DNS
data.tagline: Connect a domain name to the service that should answer
data.description: DNS translates a domain into records that direct browsers and other clients to a host, email service, or verification target. Changes may take time to spread because records are cached. Keep the required record type, name, value, and previous configuration clear before editing.

use: Point a domain to a website
avoid: Delete existing records without checking their purpose
Expect every resolver to update immediately
Mix up the record name and destination
Publish private server credentials as DNS values

lessonPractice.title: A domain was just pointed to a new server. Some people see the new site while others still see the old one. What is the safest next check?

options.label: Change the record value every few minutes until everyone sees the new site
options.feedback: Repeated edits while old caches remain create more versions and make regional results harder to diagnose.

options.label: Verify the current record and external lookup results, then account for TTL caching
options.feedback: Confirming the new record first separates a configuration error from an old cached answer and avoids unnecessary changes.

options.label: Clear one browser cache and use that result to declare the global update complete
options.feedback: Browser cache is only one layer. Recursive resolvers elsewhere may still hold the previous record.

data.agentPrompt: Results differ by location after moving the domain to a new server. Verify the current DNS record and TTL, then use external lookups to distinguish an error from old cache. Do not keep editing values. Explain what to wait for and how to confirm stable propagation.
